clue.text: Mother's turned to cooker on a boat out East

indicators.note: something turned round faces the other way, so the word is read from right to left

blocks.note: MA is mother, plus the S of the possessive
a pan is a vessel for cooking in

explanation.surface: A mother cooks on a boat somewhere in the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: A sampan is a small flat-bottomed boat used in China and Southeast Asia, hence a vessel out East.

clue.text: Eats late, making puss wild

indicators.note: a wild animal runs about unrestrained, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone dining late in the evening drives the cat into a frenzy.
explanation.definitionFit: To sup is to have supper, the light evening meal eaten late in the day.

clue.text: Cherry, extra large and not half long

indicators.note: not half means only half the word survives, the rest being thrown away

blocks.note: more means additional, extra
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
taken as written before cutting

explanation.surface: A description of a cherry that is big but not very long.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first two of the four letters of 'long' are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: The morello is a variety of sour dark cherry, often used for cooking and jam.

clue.text: A lady's first platitude is "unselfishness"

indicators.note: first points to only the opening letter of the word before it being kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the initial letter of lady
a truism is a statement so obvious it is a platitude

explanation.surface: A woman's favourite pious slogan is simply 'be unselfish'.
explanation.definitionFit: Altruism is selfless concern for the welfare of others, the opposite of selfishness.

clue.text: Felt bad having pain about a short holiday

indicators.note: something gone bad is spoilt and out of order, so the letters are reworked
about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

blocks.note: harm is injury or hurt
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone felt unwell, suffering pain throughout a brief break.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters of 'Felt' sit inside HARM. Half-term is the week-long break in the middle of a British school term.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-term is a brief school vacation partway through a term, so it is a short holiday.

clue.text: Allow account to appreciate on the shelf

blocks.note: AC is the standard abbreviation for account
to know something is to appreciate or understand it
a ledge is a narrow shelf

explanation.surface: Granting a bank account recognition when it has been left neglected on the shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: To acknowledge a claim is to admit or concede it, so it is to allow it.

clue.text: Impure base

blocks.note: first meaning: dirty, contaminated
second meaning: morally low, vile or obscene

explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' looks like a noun, a foundation, but it is an adjective meaning low or vile.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers both physical dirt and moral vileness, matching impure and base.

clue.text: Each menu is wholesome

blocks.note: EA is the abbreviation for each, as on price tags
table can mean the food provided, as in keeping a good table

explanation.surface: A restaurant boasting that every dish on offer is healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eatable is fit and good enough to eat, which loosely matches wholesome.

clue.text: An adult lawyer and a politician will be required

blocks.note: a man is an adult male
DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A grown-up, a lawyer and a politician must all be present.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mandatory is compulsory, so it is required by rule.

clue.text: Buccaneer gets very good pay

blocks.note: PI is short for pious, very good morally
a rate is a level of pay

explanation.surface: A buccaneer is rewarded with excellent wages.
explanation.walkthrough: PI for pious or virtuous is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A buccaneer was a sea robber of the Caribbean, so a synonym for pirate.

clue.text: Sketch half finished to reveal and outline

indicators.note: half finished means work stopped midway, so only the first half of the word remains

blocks.note: taken as written before cutting
to let on is to reveal a secret

explanation.surface: An artist's drawing left incomplete, exposing just its outline.
explanation.walkthrough: Only SKE, the first three of six letters, is kept from 'Sketch'.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton is a bare framework or basic plan, so it is an outline.

clue.text: Cupboard love? Certainly not!

blocks.note: surface reading: the idiom for affection shown only to get something, like a pet fawning for food
setter's reading: taken literally, a love of cupboards, and its opposite is a dread of enclosed spaces

explanation.walkthrough: Cupboard love is a British idiom for insincere affection shown in hope of reward; here it is read literally as fondness for small enclosed rooms, and its opposite is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the morbid fear of confined spaces, the reverse of liking to be shut in a cupboard.

clue.text: Most Britons could become members of a band

indicators.note: could become suggests the letters are capable of turning into something else when rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A claim that most of the British could join a musical group.
explanation.definitionFit: Trombonists play the trombone, so they are among the players in a brass band or orchestra.

clue.text: Member's devices for those sitting down

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase rather than a noun; the answer is things for seated people

blocks.note: a foot is a member, or limb, of the body, plus the possessive S
tools are devices or implements

explanation.surface: Gadgets belonging to a club member, designed for people who are seated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' here is a body part rather than a club member.
explanation.definitionFit: Footstools are low stools on which seated people rest their feet.

clue.text: Supporters will be succeeding

blocks.note: first meaning: a body of fans or adherents
second meaning: coming next, ensuing

explanation.surface: Fans of a team will go on to win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeeding' suggests winning but means coming after.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a group of fans and an adjective for what comes next.

clue.text: Note required? Give me a second

blocks.note: taken as written
a mo is a moment, a very short time

explanation.surface: Someone asked for a written message asks for a moment to write it.
explanation.walkthrough: MO, short for moment, is informal British usage, as in 'half a mo'.
explanation.definitionFit: A memo is a short written note or message, especially within an office.

clue.text: Artist who restored "Lorna Doe"

indicators.note: restored suggests something rebuilt from its parts, so the letters are put together afresh

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter who restored a picture or text named after the heroine of Lorna Doone.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci was the Italian Renaissance artist who painted the Mona Lisa.

clue.text: Alice's head freed of these insects

indicators.note: a head freed of something has lost its top, so the opening letter goes

blocks.note: the girl's name, without the possessive

explanation.surface: Alice's hair has been cleared of parasites.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is the delousing of Alice's hair; cryptically her name loses its own first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lice are small wingless parasitic insects that live in hair.

clue.text: Team wants to clip hair very short

blocks.note: a crew is a team of workers
to clip is to cut

explanation.surface: A sports team is keen to have their hair cropped close.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew cut is a very short haircut, originally worn by rowing crews.

clue.text: Old bint's eye wandering as ordered

indicators.note: wandering things stray from their path, so the letters drift into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, the possessive S ignored

explanation.surface: An old woman's gaze drifts about as instructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bint' is British slang, now offensive, for a woman. The S of the possessive is not part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something obediently means doing it in compliance with instructions, so as ordered.

clue.text: Do thank you first for trying a sample

indicators.note: first tells the solver which piece is placed at the front of the answer

blocks.note: ta is informal British for thank you
to do someone is to swindle them, and a sting is a swindle

explanation.surface: An instruction to say thanks before sampling food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like a helper verb but means cheat; the sting is placed after TA because thank you comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasting is trying a small portion of food or drink to judge its flavour.

clue.text: One very small and weak shellfish!

blocks.note: first meaning: a puny, undersized person
second meaning: the small edible crustacean

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one description of a feeble crustacean, but the person sense and the creature sense are separate.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a small edible crustacean and a disparaging term for a tiny feeble person.

clue.text: Generosity accompanies by slapping?

blocks.note: surface reading: liberality in giving
setter's reading: a slap is delivered with the palm flat and the fingers spread, so the quality literally accompanies a slap

explanation.walkthrough: The answer means liberality, but read literally it describes having the palm spread flat, as you must to slap someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Being open-handed means giving freely, so the noun is a synonym for generosity.

clue.text: First instalment of wages missing for a long time

indicators.note: the first instalment is the opening portion, pointing to the initial letter
missing means that portion is absent and has to be removed

blocks.note: taken as written before cutting

explanation.surface: A worker has gone a long while without the first part of their pay.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is adverbial; 'ages' works the same way in 'it took ages'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ages is an informal word for a very long time, as in 'I waited for ages'.

clue.text: Most irritating but not starting to be most spiteful

indicators.note: not starting means the word fails to get going, so its first letter is dropped

blocks.note: bitchy means spiteful and malicious

explanation.surface: The most annoying person is not, at first, the most malicious.
explanation.definitionFit: The itchiest thing causes the most itching, so it is the most irritating to the skin.

clue.text: Fish head when cut off becomes loose

indicators.note: cutting off a head removes the top, so the opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: a herring is a common sea fish

explanation.surface: A fish whose head is removed comes free.
explanation.definitionFit: Erring means straying from the right path, so morally loose or wayward.

clue.text: Between you, me and this, pottages need stirring

indicators.note: stirring a pot mixes its contents, so the letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A confidential cooking tip that thick soups must be stirred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Between you, me and the gatepost' is a British idiom meaning in confidence; 'this' stands for the answer. Pottage is thick soup or stew.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a post as the third party to a secret, so the answer completes the phrase.

clue.text: Ugh! It's in the lettuce. One of them should attract attention

definitions.text: One of them should attract attention
definitions.note: defines the plural answer by describing one member of the set

indicators.note: something in another sits inside it, so one word is placed within the other

blocks.note: cos is a variety of lettuce, also called romaine
taken as written

explanation.surface: Disgust at finding something in the salad, and an aside about getting noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: Cos is a long-leafed lettuce; the exclamation goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A discreet cough is a common way to draw someone's attention.
